title: Q1 - Flashing Red Light
question_text: A flashing red traffic light means:
opt1: Stop, yield to traffic, and proceed when safe.
opt2: Slow down and proceed with caution.
opt3: Come to a complete stop and wait for a green light.
opt4: Stop only if there is cross traffic.
explanation: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign – stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

title: Q2 - Diamond Sign
question_text: A diamond-shaped sign indicates:
opt3: Warning or hazard ahead.
explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow and warn of hazards or unusual conditions ahead.

title: Q3 - Solid Yellow Line (Your Side)
question_text: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
opt3: You are in a construction zone.
opt4: You are approaching a school zone.
explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass – it is a no-passing zone.

title: Q4 - Pennant Sign Shape
question_text: A sign shaped like a pennant (pointed sideways) indicates a:
opt3: No passing zone.
explanation: A pennant-shaped sign always marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.

title: Q5 - Flashing Yellow Signal
question_text: What should you do at a flashing yellow traffic signal?
opt1: Stop completely before entering the intersection.
opt2: Slow down and proceed with caution.
opt3: Maintain speed but look both ways.
opt4: Treat it as a stop sign.
explanation: Flashing yellow means proceed with caution – be alert for hazards.

title: Q6 - Orange Sign Color
question_text: An orange-colored sign always indicates:
opt3: A regulatory command.
explanation: Orange signs are used exclusively for construction and maintenance zones.

title: Q7 - School Zone Sign Shape
question_text: A school zone sign is what shape?
opt3: Diamond.
explanation: School zone signs are pentagon-shaped (five sides).

title: Q8 - White Pavement Lines at Intersections
question_text: White lines painted across the pavement at intersections indicate:
opt1: Where vehicles must stop for signs or signals.
opt2: The zone where parking is permitted.
opt3: A pedestrian-only walking path.
opt4: Where you must yield to bicycles.
explanation: Solid white stop lines show where to stop for signs or red lights.

title: Q9 - Steady Red Arrow
question_text: What does a steady red arrow mean?
opt1: You can turn carefully after stopping.
opt2: You must full stop and cannot turn in the direction of the arrow.
opt3: You have the right-of-way to turn.
opt4: You must yield to pedestrians only.
explanation: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not turn in that direction.

title: Q10 - Round Yellow RR Sign
question_text: A round yellow sign with a black "X" and the letters "RR" warns of:
opt3: A rough road surface.
explanation: This is the advance warning sign for a railroad crossing.

title: Q11 - Broken White Lines
question_text: Broken white lines on the pavement mean:
opt1: Traffic is moving in opposite directions.
opt3: Traffic is moving in the same direction, and you may change lanes safely.
explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction – you may cross them to change lanes.

title: Q12 - Yield Sign Shape
question_text: A yield sign is shaped like a:
opt3: Rectangle.
explanation: Yield signs are downward-pointing triangles.

title: Q13 - Red with White Bar
question_text: A red sign with a white horizontal bar across the middle reads:
opt3: Wrong Way.
explanation: That is the "Do Not Enter" sign – you must not enter that roadway.

title: Q14 - Red Circle with Slash
question_text: If you see a regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash over a symbol, it means:
opt3: You must use caution performing the action.
opt4: The action is allowed only during certain hours.
explanation: The red circle with a slash means "No" – the action is prohibited.

title: Q15 - Double Solid Yellow Lines
question_text: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?
opt1: Passing is allowed for vehicles on both sides.
opt2: Vehicles traveling in both directions are forbidden from passing.
opt3: You can pass if the road ahead is clear for 500 feet.
opt4: You may cross to make a U-turn.
explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction.

title: Q16 - Residential Speed Limit
question_text: Unless otherwise posted, the standard speed limit in a Florida residential area is:
opt3: 45 mph.
explanation: Florida law sets residential areas at 30 mph unless posted otherwise.

title: Q17 - Interstate Maximum Speed
question_text: What is the maximum speed limit on a Florida interstate highway under ideal conditions?
opt3: 70 mph.
explanation: The maximum speed limit on Florida interstates is 70 mph.

title: Q18 - Speed in Fog/Rain
question_text: If a speed limit is posted at 55 mph, but the weather is foggy and rainy, you should:
opt1: Drive 55 mph since it is the legal limit.
opt2: Slow down below 55 mph to match the safe driving conditions.
opt3: Drive with your high beams on at 55 mph.
opt4: Drive in the left lane to avoid puddles.
explanation: You must adjust your speed to weather conditions – slow down in rain/fog.

title: Q19 - Slower Traffic Lane
question_text: When driving slower than the flow of traffic on a multi-lane highway, you should use:
opt3: The middle lane.
explanation: Slower traffic must keep right and use the right lane.

title: Q20 - Two-Second Rule
question_text: The "two-second rule" applies to:
opt1: How long you should stop at a stop sign.
opt2: The safe following distance under good weather conditions.
opt3: The time required to signal before a turn.
opt4: The time to check your blind spot.
explanation: The two-second rule helps maintain a safe following distance (now 4 seconds recommended).

title: Q21 - Entering Interstate from Ramp
question_text: When entering an interstate highway from an acceleration lane, you should:
opt1: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for an opening.
opt2: Match the speed of interstate traffic and merge safely.
opt3: Yield to all highway traffic by stopping on the ramp.
opt4: Signal and wait for a gap, then accelerate.
explanation: Merge at highway speed – do not stop unless traffic is too heavy.

title: Q22 - Signal Distance Before Turn
question_text: In Florida, you must signal your intention to turn at least how many feet before turning?
opt3: 200 feet.
explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning.

title: Q23 - Passing Near Bridge/Tunnel
question_text: It is illegal to pass another vehicle within how many feet of a bridge, tunnel, or railroad crossing?
opt3: 150 feet.
explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of bridges, tunnels, and railroad crossings.

title: Q24 - Four-Way Stop Tie
question_text: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop intersection at the same time, who yields?
opt1: The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
opt2: The driver on the right yields to the driver on the left.
opt3: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
opt4: The first to honk goes first.
explanation: At a four-way stop, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

title: Q25 - HOV Lanes
question_text: HOV lanes on interstates are reserved for:
opt1: Vehicles carrying multiple occupants, buses, or motorcycles.
opt2: Heavy trucks and commercial cargo vehicles.
opt3: High-speed vehicles passing others.
explanation: HOV lanes are for high-occupancy vehicles, buses, and motorcycles.

title: Q26 - Passing on the Right
question_text: You may pass on the right side of another vehicle only if:
opt1: The vehicle ahead is making a right turn.
opt2: There are two or more lanes of traffic moving in your direction.
opt3: You drive onto the unpaved shoulder of the road.
opt4: The vehicle ahead is stopped for a pedestrian.
explanation: Passing on the right is legal only when there are two or more lanes in your direction.

title: Q27 - Minimum Interstate Speed
question_text: What is the minimum speed limit on Florida interstate highways under normal conditions?
opt3: 50 mph.
explanation: The minimum speed on interstates is 50 mph when the limit is 70 mph.

title: Q28 - Missed Exit
question_text: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, you should:
opt1: Back up carefully on the shoulder.
opt2: Make a U-turn across the median grass.
opt3: Go to the next exit and pull off there.
opt4: Stop and wait for a gap to reverse.
explanation: Never back up – continue to the next exit and turn around safely.

title: Q29 - Center Lane (Solid + Broken Yellow)
question_text: Center lanes bordered by a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line are used for:
opt3: Emergency parking only.
explanation: These are center turn lanes – only for left turns from either direction.

title: Q30 - Left Turn from One-Way to One-Way
question_text: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should turn from:
opt3: The far left lane.
explanation: Turn from the far left lane when going from one-way to one-way.

title: Q31 - Move Over Law
question_text: Florida's "Move Over" law requires drivers approaching law enforcement or emergency vehicles stopped on the roadside to:
opt1: Maintain speed but honk to notify them.
opt2: Vacate the lane closest to the vehicle, or slow down to 20 mph below the posted limit.
opt3: Stop immediately in the roadway.
opt4: Move to the shoulder and stop.
explanation: Vacate the closest lane, or slow to 20 mph below the limit if you cannot move over.

title: Q32 - Under 21 DUI Limit
question_text: In Florida, a person under 21 is considered legally DUI if their Blood Alcohol Level (BAL) is:
opt3: 0.08% or higher.
explanation: Zero tolerance for under 21 – .02% or higher triggers suspension.

title: Q33 - 21+ DUI Limit
question_text: For drivers 21 and older, the legal limit for Blood Alcohol Level (BAL) is:
explanation: The legal limit for drivers 21+ is .08%.

title: Q34 - Implied Consent Law
question_text: Under Florida's "Implied Consent" law, by signing a driver license application, you agree to:
opt1: Keep insurance on your vehicle at all times.
opt2: Take a chemical test (breath, blood, or urine) if suspected of driving under the influence.
opt3: Allow passengers to drink alcohol in your vehicle.
opt4: Submit to a vehicle search upon request.
explanation: Implied consent means you agree to chemical testing if suspected of DUI.

title: Q35 - School Bus - Painted Turn Lane
question_text: If a school bus stops on a multi-lane highway divided only by a painted turn lane, who must stop?
opt1: Only vehicles behind the school bus.
opt3: No one is required to stop if there are four or more lanes.
opt4: Only vehicles approaching from the front.
explanation: A painted turn lane is not a physical barrier – all directions must stop.

title: Q36 - School Bus - Raised Median
question_text: If a school bus stops on a highway separated by a raised unpaved median at least 5 feet wide, who must stop?
opt1: Only vehicles traveling in the same direction as the bus.
opt3: No one is required to stop.
opt4: Only vehicles in the opposite direction.
explanation: A raised median 5+ feet wide means only same-direction traffic must stop.

title: Q37 - Front-Seat Seat Belt
question_text: In Florida, front-seat passengers must wear a seat belt if they are:
opt2: All ages must wear a seat belt.
opt3: Only if the vehicle has an airbag.
opt4: Only if the vehicle is moving over 40 mph.
explanation: All front-seat passengers of any age must wear a seat belt.

title: Q38 - Child Restraint Age
question_text: Children under what age must be secured in a crash-tested, federally approved child restraint device?
opt3: Under 8 years old.
explanation: Florida law requires children 5 and under to be in a safety seat or booster.

title: Q39 - Address Change Notification
question_text: If you change your address within Florida, you must notify the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles within:
opt3: 45 days.
explanation: You have 30 calendar days to update your address.

title: Q40 - Texting While Driving
question_text: Texting while driving is legal in Florida only when:
opt1: Stopped at a red traffic light.
opt2: Driving on a rural road with no traffic.
opt3: Texting while driving is illegal at all times while the vehicle is in motion.
opt4: If you are using a mounted device for navigation.
explanation: Texting while driving is illegal at all times when the vehicle is in motion.

title: Q41 - Minor Crash Blocking Traffic
question_text: If you are involved in a minor crash that blocks traffic, Florida law requires you to:
opt1: Leave the vehicle exactly where it is until police arrive.
opt2: Move your vehicle off the roadway if it can be safely driven.
opt3: Wait for a tow truck to move it.
opt4: Leave the scene to call for help.
explanation: Move your vehicle off the roadway if it is drivable to clear traffic.

title: Q42 - Florida Insurance Requirements
question_text: What are the two main types of auto insurance required under Florida's Financial Responsibility Law?
opt2: Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL).
opt3: Uninsured Motorist and Medical Payments.
explanation: PIP ($10k) and PDL ($10k) are the required coverages.

title: Q43 - Reinstatement for Child Support Suspension
question_text: If your driver's license is suspended for failing to pay child support, you can reinstate it by:
opt2: Paying a reinstatement fee and showing proof the matter is resolved.
opt3: Retaking the written test.
explanation: Resolve the child support issue and pay the reinstatement fee.

title: Q44 - Documents During Traffic Stop
question_text: If a law enforcement officer stops you, you must show:
opt3: Driver's license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.
opt4: Driver's license and proof of insurance only.
explanation: You must show driver license, registration, and proof of insurance.

title: Q45 - Dim High Beams - Oncoming
question_text: High beam headlights must be dimmed when an oncoming vehicle is within:
opt3: 1,000 feet.
explanation: Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

title: Q46 - Dim High Beams - Following
question_text: Your high beam headlights must be dimmed when you are following another vehicle within:
opt3: 500 feet.
explanation: Dim high beams within 300 feet when following another vehicle.

title: Q47 - Lights in Rain/Fog
question_text: When driving in heavy rain or fog, you should turn on your:
opt3: Hazard lights (flashers) only.
explanation: Low beams improve visibility – high beams reflect off fog/rain and reduce visibility.

title: Q48 - Hydroplaning Action
question_text: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (glide on a film of water), you should:
opt3: Take your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.
explanation: Ease off the gas, do not brake, and steer gently.

title: Q49 - Uphill Parking (with curb)
question_text: When parking uphill against a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
opt3: Straight ahead.
explanation: Uphill with curb: turn wheels away from the curb.

title: Q50 - Downhill Parking (with curb)
question_text: When parking downhill against a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
opt3: Straight ahead.
explanation: Downhill: turn wheels toward the curb.

title: Q51 - Defensive Driving
question_text: Defensive driving means:
opt1: Constantly defending your position in your lane.
opt2: Staying alert and anticipating the mistakes of other drivers.
opt3: Driving under the minimum speed limit to remain safe.
opt4: Driving with your hands at 10 and 2 at all times.
explanation: Defensive driving is about being alert and anticipating others' actions.

title: Q52 - Blind Spots
question_text: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that:
opt1: You can see clearly in your rearview mirror.
opt2: Cannot be seen in your mirrors and require turning your head to check.
opt3: Are blocked by passengers in the back seat.
opt4: Are only present on the left side.
explanation: Blind spots require you to turn your head to check before changing lanes.

title: Q53 - Large Truck Blind Spots
question_text: Large commercial trucks have large blind spots called:
opt3: Danger zones.
explanation: No-Zones are the blind spots around large trucks.

title: Q54 - Headlight Times
question_text: You must turn on your vehicle's headlights between:
opt3: One hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.
explanation: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise.

title: Q55 - Right Wheels Off Pavement
question_text: If your right wheels drop off the paved edge of the road, you should:
opt1: Jerk the steering wheel hard to the left.
opt2: Slow down, ease off the gas, and steer gently back onto the pavement.
opt3: Press the brake firmly to come to a sudden stop.
opt4: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right.
explanation: Ease off the gas, brake lightly, and steer gently back.

title: Q56 - Tire Blowout
question_text: If your vehicle suffers a tire blowout, you should:
opt1: Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the gas, and brake gently.
opt2: Pump the brakes rapidly and turn off the road.
opt3: Shift into neutral and apply the emergency brake.
opt4: Slam on the brakes to stop quickly.
explanation: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off gas, brake gently when under control.

title: Q57 - Bicyclist Rights
question_text: Bicyclists riding on a public roadway have:
opt1: The same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers.
opt2: No rights on the roadway and must yield to all cars.
opt3: The right to ride on sidewalks only.
explanation: Bicycles are legally vehicles and have the same rights/duties.

title: Q58 - Sharing Lane with Motorcyclist
question_text: When sharing the lane with a motorcyclist, you must give them:
opt3: Motorcyclists do not have lane rights.
opt4: At least 3 feet within the same lane.
explanation: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full lane – do not share.

title: Q59 - White Cane / Guide Dog
question_text: If you are stopped at a red light and a pedestrian carrying a white cane or a guide dog steps into the crosswalk, you must:
opt1: Honk your horn to warn them.
opt3: Yield the right-of-way and remain stopped until they cross.
explanation: Yield to pedestrians with white canes or guide dogs – they are visually impaired.

title: Q60 - Drowsy Driving Effect
question_text: Driving while tired or drowsy can:
opt2: Have a similar negative impact on your driving skills as alcohol.
opt3: Be fixed completely by turning up the radio volume.
opt4: Only affects your vision, not reaction.
explanation: Drowsy driving is as dangerous as drunk driving – it slows reaction and judgment.
